housing: Wakefield district combines the city with former mining and mill towns such as Castleford, Pontefract, Normanton, Ossett and the south-east coalfield villages. Housing is dominated by Victorian and early 20th-century brick terraces and large post-war council estates, now partly privately let after right to buy. Private renting is below the regional average but grew between 2011 and 2021, with lets concentrated in central terraces such as Agbrigg. The council has used an Article 4 Direction to control small HMOs in parts of the district.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Agbrigg, Belle Vue and Castleford: photograph back yards, cellar walls and any damp low on the walls.
Former colliery homes in Hemsworth and South Elmsall: note any cracks in walls and record the mining report if one was supplied.
Former council houses bought under right to buy: check window seals, boiler cupboards and any non-standard construction noted on the paperwork.
Mill and office conversions in Wakefield centre: record fob counts, parking, bin store access and window ventilation.
Homes near the Calder and Aire in Castleford and Horbury: check ground floors and walls for damp or past flood marks.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can contact Wakefield Council's Housing Standards team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions.
